request: An adapter plate to screw a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B onto the back of a monitor through its VESA 75 mount (75 x 75 mm hole pattern, M4 screws).

body_sources.w: https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpi4/raspberry-pi-4-mechanical-drawing.pdf top dimension '85' (same drawing as Figure 1 'Mechanical Dimensions' in the Pi 4 datasheet RP-008341)
body_sources.h: https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpi4/raspberry-pi-4-mechanical-drawing.pdf tallest part label 'Z=16.0' on both USB stacks. The drawing does not say whether Z counts the PCB and gives no board thickness, so the real top may sit higher; h only places the open +z face

features.name: mount_hole_front_left
features.source: drawing: hole center '3.5' from the left edge and '3.5' from the front edge, hole diameter '2.7' (callouts '6' and '2.7' at the hole by the micro HDMI ports); u = 85 - 3.5

features.name: mount_hole_front_right
features.source: drawing: '3.5' plus hole spacing '58' along x gives x 61.5, '3.5' from the front edge, diameter '2.7'; u = 85 - 61.5

features.name: mount_hole_back_left
features.source: drawing: '3.5' from the left edge, '3.5' plus hole spacing '49' along y gives y 52.5 (also '3.5' from the back edge), diameter '2.7'; u = 85 - 3.5

why: Pi 4 lying component side up on the plate (+z up, -z against the plate and monitor): tests an adapter that screws the board through its four 2.7 mm holes (58 x 49 mm) and carries the VESA MIS-D 75 pattern, 75 x 75 mm +/- 0.25 mm for M4 x 0.7 screws (VESA FDMI v1.1 sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.3), with the top left clear.
